subject: Food Science
title: Yeast Spoilage
description: A quick win: understand Yeast Spoilage.

hook.text: That fizzy, alcoholic taste in old orange juice? Wild yeast fermented the sugars while the bottle sat in your fridge.

buildup.text: Yeasts are single-celled fungi that thrive on sugars. They're everywhere—on fruit skins, in the air, on surfaces.

discovery.text: Saccharomyces and Zygosaccharomyces are common food spoilers. They ferment sugars into alcohol, CO₂, and off-flavors.

twist.text: Some spoilage yeasts tolerate high sugar and low pH—surviving in jam, syrup, and fruit juice that kills most bacteria.

climax.text: Pasteurization kills yeasts in juice. Without it, unpasteurized cider can turn alcoholic on the shelf.

punchline.text: Yeast turns sugar into alcohol. Sometimes that's beer. Sometimes it's spoiled juice.

quiz.question: Why does unpasteurized cider sometimes become alcoholic?
options: Wild yeasts ferment the sugars into alcohol
